newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arabs say Israel hell-bent on smashing peace.
newsitem.headline: Arabs say Israel hell-bent on smashing peace.

text.p: Arabs on Thursday said Israel was determined to wreck the Middle East peace process by opening a tunnel under Islam's third holiest site in Jerusalem and warned it alone would suffer the dire consequences of this provocation.

Twenty Palestinians and two Israelis have so far been killed in two days of clashes in the self-rule areas of the West Bank and Gaza Strip sparked by the tunnel's opening beside the Temple Mount at Jerusalem, site of the al-Aqsa mosque.

"It is as if (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu is eagerly triggering a conflict in order to write off the Oslo (peace) agreement and to reverse whatever has been achieved on the basis of this 1993 pact," the Gulf News daily newspaper of the United Arab Emirates said.
"Instead of persuading the European leaders that he is committed to peace, he has only succeeded in convincing them that he is hell-bent on bringing disaster to the Middle East."

Relations between the Palestinians and Netanyahu's hardline government have been on the slide since his election 100 days ago on a platform that rejects the "land for peace" principle, a basis of the peace process launched in Madrid in 1991.
Arab governments have slammed Netanyahu for lifting a ban on building Jewish settlements in the Palestinian self rule areas and delaying the redeployment of troops from the West Bank town of Hebron.

The opening of the tunnel was the latest in what Arabs have called Israel's attempts to "Judaise" Jerusalem and could set the drums of a new Arab-Israeli war beating, Egypt's official Al-Ahram said in an editorial.
"The goverment of Netanyahu insists on carrying through actions that will reignite an Arab Israeli conflict," the government-owned daily said.
"Expanding the tunnel... is a blatant violation of Islam's holy sites. Does Israel want to impose a de facto policy to get what it wants without resorting to the negotiating table?"
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak told Netanyahu that the violence will only stop when Israel fulfills its agreements with the Palestinians, the state's spokesman said on Wednesday.

"If Israel thinks Arabs will not act, then the region will return to what it was before negotiations... These intransigent positions are putting the whole region into a volcano which could erupt at any moment and Israel will probably be the biggest -- and only -- loser," the newspaper added.
Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority asked Arab governments at an emergency meeting of the Arab League on Thursday to isolate and punish Israel for its "perverse aggressive behaviour".

Arab foreign ministers meeting in Cairo two weeks ago said they had drafted a plan of action which might include reconsidering ties with Israeli unless it makes progress on regional peace talks, a step which the UAE's al-Khaleej daily called for in a Thursday editorial.

"It is time that Arab capitals close their doors to the leaders of Israel and their envoys... it is time to freeze what is called multilateral negotiations until bilateral negotiations clarify the white from the black," the newspaper said.

Tunisia and Algeria -- former and current head of the 22-member Arab League -- called on the world and particularly the sponsors of the peace process, the United States and Russia, to pressure the Jewish state to keep its pledges.

"Algeria calls on the international community to act to preserve the character of Islam's holy places and the national rights of the Palestinian people in Jerusalem," the Algerian foreign ministry said in a statement echoed by Tunisia.

Jordan and Qatar have also condemned Israel's opening of a tunnel, the official Qatari news agency said, adding that the leaders of both states which share ties with Israel held it responsible for this "provocation of Arab and Moslem feelings."
